headline: Bolivia Marks First Year of Reforms With Currency Float and IMF Deal
summary: President Rodrigo Paz marked his first year leading Bolivia, navigating fuel price liberalization, a floating exchange rate, an IMF agreement, and friction with labor unions and prosecutors.
why: Bolivia's shift away from fixed exchange rates and fuel subsidies is a key macro turning point for Andean sovereign debt and regional energy trade.

impacts.name: Bolivian Boliviano
impacts.why: President Paz introduced a floating currency and freed fuel prices under an IMF framework.
